import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FiniteDimensional.Basic
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.RightExactness

/-!
# Rank-one fibre quotients

If a vector `1 ⊗ s` is nonzero in a one-dimensional fibre `K ⊗[B] M`, then it spans that
fibre.  Consequently, every surjective image of `M` that kills `s` has zero `K`-fibre.

The mapped-submodule form is tailored to an ideal `J ≤ B`: if the fibre of `J` has rank one,
`s ∈ J` survives in that fibre, and a quotient map kills `s`, then the image of `J` in the
quotient has zero residue-field fibre.  This is purely right exactness of tensor product;
neither flatness nor finite generation over `B` is needed at this step.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace RankOneFibre

/-- A surjective image has zero field fibre when every source-fibre vector is a scalar multiple
of `1 ⊗ s`, and the image kills `s`.  The spanning hypothesis also covers the zero-fibre case;
no dimension or nonzero-vector assumption is required. -/
theorem subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton
    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (s : M)
    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, ∃ c : K, c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s) = v)
    (hfs : f s = 0) :
    Subsingleton (N ⊗[B] K) := by
  have hft : Function.Surjective (f.lTensor K) :=
    LinearMap.lTensor_surjective K hf
  have hzero : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, (f.lTensor K) v = 0 := by
    intro v
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hspan v
    rw [← hc, ← TensorProduct.tmul_eq_smul_one_tmul c s,
      LinearMap.lTensor_tmul, hfs]
    simp
  have hsub : Subsingleton (K ⊗[B] N) := by
    refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨x', rfl⟩ := hft x
    obtain ⟨y', rfl⟩ := hft y
    rw [hzero x', hzero y']
  exact (TensorProduct.comm B N K).toEquiv.subsingleton

/-- A surjective image of a module has zero field fibre if it kills a nonzero vector spanning
the one-dimensional source fibre. -/
theorem subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one
    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (s : M)
    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    Subsingleton (N ⊗[B] K) := by
  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton f hf s
  intro v
  exact exists_smul_eq_of_finrank_eq_one hfin hs v
  exact hfs

/-- If a linear map kills a generator of a one-dimensional source fibre, the fibre of its
range is zero. -/
theorem subsingleton_range_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M)
    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    Subsingleton ((LinearMap.range f) ⊗[B] K) := by
  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one f.rangeRestrict
    (LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict f) s hfin hs
  apply Subtype.ext
  exact hfs

/-- Range specialization of `subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton`. -/
theorem subsingleton_range_tensor_of_span_singleton
    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M)
    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, ∃ c : K, c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s) = v)
    (hfs : f s = 0) :
    Subsingleton ((LinearMap.range f) ⊗[B] K) := by
  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton f.rangeRestrict
    (LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict f) s hspan
  apply Subtype.ext
  exact hfs

/-- Let `P` be a submodule whose field fibre is one-dimensional.  If `s ∈ P` survives in
that fibre and `f s = 0`, then the fibre of the image `f(P)` is zero.

For a chart ideal `J` and the quotient map `B → B/(s)`, the conclusion is precisely the
vanishing of the fibre of the image of `J` in `B/(s)`. -/
theorem subsingleton_map_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (P : Submodule B M) (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M) (hsP : s ∈ P)
    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] P) = 1)
    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] K) := by
  rw [← LinearMap.range_domRestrict P f]
  apply subsingleton_range_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
    (f.domRestrict P) (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) hfin hs
  simpa using hfs

/-- Mapped-submodule specialization of `subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton`.
This is useful when the source ideal fibre may itself be zero. -/
theorem subsingleton_map_tensor_of_span_singleton
    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (P : Submodule B M) (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M) (hsP : s ∈ P)
    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] P, ∃ c : K,
      c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P)) = v) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] K) := by
  rw [← LinearMap.range_domRestrict P f]
  apply subsingleton_range_tensor_of_span_singleton
    (f.domRestrict P) (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) hspan
  simpa using hfs

/-- Quotienting by a vector that survives and spans a one-dimensional field fibre produces
a quotient with zero field fibre. -/
theorem subsingleton_quotient_span_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
    {B K M : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M]
    (s : M) (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) :
    Subsingleton ((M ⧸ Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)) ⊗[B] K) := by
  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one
    (Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)).mkQ
    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _) s hfin hs
  rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
  exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self s

end RankOneFibre

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# DAT-C C2 — the rank-1 H⁰ export and the generator kit
(`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-3 Σ-RANK1, §2 (N1)/(N3))

On the fibrewise h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization
`χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`, the datum engine's `H⁰` is an **invertible** module: finite,
projective, and of stalk-rank exactly `1`.  This is the rank export the engine
(`datumRigidEngine`, `Cohomology/GluedSheafEngine.lean`) leaves open — it delivers
finite + projective, never `rankAtStalk = 1`.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_relCurve` — the χ transport `χ(𝒪_{C_L}) = 1 − n` to every
  field `L` of the test tower (base-field invariance of the genus, `chi_moduleKSheaf`
  + `genus_baseField`; a re-derivation of the private lemma of `DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one` — **the fibre
  computation**: for a datum whose fibre class over `L` has `classDeg = n`, with `H¹` of
  the base-changed sheaf vanishing, `h⁰(C_L, F_{D_L}) = 1` — the Riemann–Roch anchor
  `h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi` (`n + (1 − n)`) read through the presentation
  bridge `presentationSheafIso`.  The fibre geometric package is threaded as instance
  arguments (`Curve.BaseChangeInstances`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one` — **Σ-RANK1,
  the datum-level export**: on the vanishing locus (fibre degree `n`, `χ = 1 − n`),
  `Module.rankAtStalk (H⁰(F_D)) p = 1`.  Route: `Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as
  the `κ(p)`-fibre dimension; `datumH0BaseChange` (on the nose) identifies the fibre with
  `H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`; the fibre computation above pins it at `1`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one` — the
  certified-family specialization (**N1**): for `G` landing in the h¹-vanishing locus
  `V`, the divisor datum `D_G := G.adaptation.divisorDatum` has invertible `H⁰`.  The
  fibre-degree hypothesis is discharged uniformly by `DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass` (the
  fibre class has `classDeg = n` at every field).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily.exists_fibrewise_generator_divisorDatum`
  — **N3, the generator kit**: since `H⁰(F_{D_G})` is projective of rank `1` (hence has a
  nontrivial fibre at every prime of the locus), a fibrewise-nonzero **global** section
  exists Zariski-locally (`Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`).

Noetherian discipline (worksheet §2): every rank statement carries `[IsNoetherianRing S]`
through the engine; the arbitrary-test consumers reach it through RE-5 stages.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian Scheme

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {n : ℕ}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-- The standing `C.left`-over-`k` structure, keyed on `C.hom` — the instance the base
χ-normalization `hχ : χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n` is phrased against (defeq to `.ofHom C.hom`, so
`chi_moduleKSheaf C` unifies with it). -/
noncomputable local instance instOverCleftRankOne : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩

/-! ## The χ transport to the fibre curve -/

/-- **`χ(𝒪) = 1 − n` at every field extension**, from the base normalization
(`chi_moduleKSheaf` at the base-changed bundle + `genus_baseField`; a re-derivation of the
`DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel` private lemma). -/
theorem chi_relCurve (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    Sheaf.chi ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (n : ℤ) := by
  haveI : IsProper (baseChangeBundle C L).hom := instIsProperSndLeft C L
  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (baseChangeBundle C L).hom :=
    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft C L
  haveI : GeometricallyIrreducible (baseChangeBundle C L).hom :=
    instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft C L
  have h1 : Sheaf.chi ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L)
      = 1 - (genus (baseChangeBundle C L) : ℤ) := chi_moduleKSheaf (baseChangeBundle C L)
  have h2 : genus (baseChangeBundle C L) = genus C := genus_baseField C L
  have h3 : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (genus C : ℤ) := chi_moduleKSheaf C
  have h4 : (genus C : ℤ) = (n : ℤ) := by rw [h3] at hχ; linarith
  rw [h1, h2, h4]

/-! ## The fibre computation: `h⁰(C_L, F_{D_L}) = 1`

The fibre geometric instances (`Curve.BaseChangeInstances`) are threaded as instance
arguments — they cannot be synthesized through the `relCurve` `def` barrier, so consumers
install them by `haveI` (the `degAt_abelDiv` block, I-0249 (iv)) before calling. -/

/-- **The fibre h⁰ pin**: for a datum whose fibre class over the field `L` has
`classDeg = n`, with the base χ-normalization and vanishing `H¹` of the base-changed
sheaf, the fibre global-section count is exactly `1` — the Riemann–Roch rank anchor
`h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi` read through the presentation bridge
`presentationSheafIso`, at `n + (1 − n)`. -/
theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C S π)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra S L] [IsScalarTower k S L]
    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
    (hg : classDeg L (D.baseChange L).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ))
    (hsub : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange L).sheaf 1)) :
    Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf = 1 := by
  set P : (relCurve C L).MeromorphicPresentation :=
    Scheme.MeromorphicPresentation.ofCocycle (D.baseChange L).pointedCover
      (gluedSubordCocycle (D.baseChange L).isGluingCocycle
        (D.baseChange L).pointedCover (D.baseChange L).pieceIndex
        fun _ => le_rfl) with hP
  have hsubP : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (P.gluedSheaf L) 1) :=
    (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L)) 1).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mp
      hsub
  have h0eq : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf = Sheaf.h0 (P.gluedSheaf L) :=
    Sheaf.h0_congr (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L))
  have hformula := h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi L P hsubP
  have hPclass : P.picClass = (D.baseChange L).cechPicClass := rfl
  have hint : (Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf : ℤ) = 1 := by
    rw [h0eq, hformula, hPclass, hg, chi_relCurve hχ L]; ring
  exact_mod_cast hint

/-! ## Σ-RANK1: the rank-1 export on the vanishing locus -/

/-- **Σ-RANK1, the datum-level rank export** (worksheet GAP-3): on the fibrewise
h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization `χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`,
the datum engine's `H⁰` has stalk-rank exactly `1` at `p`.

`Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as the `κ(p)`-dimension of the fibre
`κ(p) ⊗[S] H⁰`; the on-the-nose base change `datumH0BaseChange` identifies this fibre with
`H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`, whose dimension is `1` by the fibre computation. The global
fibrewise hypothesis `hfib` supplies finiteness/projectivity (hence flatness) through
`datumRigidEngine`. -/
theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C S π) [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
    (hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
      Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
    [QuasiCompact
      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)]
    (hg : classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ)) :
    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨-, hfin, hproj⟩ := datumRigidEngine D hπ hfib
  haveI := hfin
  haveI := hproj
  have hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1 := datum_subsingleton_pairH1 D hπ hfib
  have hfibre : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf = 1 :=
    D.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one hχ p.asIdeal.ResidueField hg
      (D.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1)
  calc Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p
      = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
          (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)) :=
        Module.rankAtStalk_eq p
    _ = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
          (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf 0) :=
        (D.datumH0BaseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1).finrank_eq
    _ = Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf := rfl
    _ = 1 := hfibre

/-! ## The certified-family specialization: N1 (invertible `H⁰`) and N3 (generators) -/

omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
/-- (Implementation) The fibre class of the divisor datum has `classDeg = n` at `κ(p)`:
the base change of `G.eqns`, read through `DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass`. -/
private theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.classDeg_baseChange_divisorDatum
    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
    [QuasiCompact
      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)] :
    classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (G.adaptation.divisorDatum.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ) := by
  have hcl : G.adaptation.divisorDatum.cechPicClass = (DivFam.mk G).toZar.picClass := by
    rw [G.adaptation.cechPicClass_divisorDatum, DivFamZar.picClass_toZar, DivFam.picClass_mk]
  rw [G.adaptation.divisorDatum.cechPicClass_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField, hcl,
    ← DivFamZar.picClass_mapAlg]
  exact DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass
    (DivFamZar.mapAlg p.asIdeal.ResidueField n (DivFam.mk G).toZar)

/-- **N1 — invertibility of the canonical `H⁰`** (worksheet §2 (N1)): for a certified
divisor family `G` landing in the h¹-vanishing locus `V` (`hvan`), the divisor datum
`D_G := G.adaptation.divisorDatum` has `H⁰` of stalk-rank exactly `1` at every prime.

The fibre-degree hypothesis of `rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one` is discharged uniformly:
the fibre class of `D_G` at `κ(p)` is the base change of `G.eqns`, which has
`classDeg = n` at every field (`DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass`). -/
theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one
    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
    (hvan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S, (DivFam.mk G).toZar.IsH1VanishingAt p)
    (p : PrimeSpectrum S) :
    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
  have hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
      Subsingleton ((datumPair G.adaptation.divisorDatum).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
    fun q => (G.isH1VanishingAt_toZar_iff q).mp (hvan q)
  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
  haveI : QuasiCompact
      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
  exact G.adaptation.divisorDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one hπ hχ hfib p
    (G.classDeg_baseChange_divisorDatum p)

/-- **N3 — the generator kit** (worksheet §2 (N3)): since `H⁰(F_{D_G})` is projective of
stalk-rank `1` on the locus, its `κ(p)`-fibre is nontrivial, so a fibrewise-nonzero
**global** section exists on a basic open `D(f) ∋ p` — the Zariski-local generator
(`Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`, the Nakayama-neighbourhood kit of
`Picard/LocalGenerators.lean`). -/
theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.exists_fibrewise_generator_divisorDatum
    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
    (hvan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S, (DivFam.mk G).toZar.IsH1VanishingAt p)
    (p : PrimeSpectrum S) :
    ∃ f : S, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ ∃ q : Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0,
      ∀ q' : PrimeSpectrum S, f ∉ q'.asIdeal →
        (q ⊗ₜ (1 : q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
            Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0 ⊗[S] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 := by
  have hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
      Subsingleton ((datumPair G.adaptation.divisorDatum).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
    fun q => (G.isH1VanishingAt_toZar_iff q).mp (hvan q)
  obtain ⟨-, hfin, hproj⟩ := datumRigidEngine G.adaptation.divisorDatum hπ hfib
  haveI := hfin
  haveI := hproj
  have hrank : Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
    G.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one hπ hχ hvan p
  -- rank 1 ⟹ the `κ(p)`-fibre is nontrivial
  have hfr : Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) = 1 := by
    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq]; exact hrank
  haveI : Nontrivial (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S]
      Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) :=
    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos (by rw [hfr]; norm_num)
  have hnt : Nontrivial (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0 ⊗[S]
      p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
    (TensorProduct.comm S _ _).toEquiv.symm.nontrivial
  exact Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective p hnt

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# Rank-one fibre reduction for the chart colength

This is the geometric wrapper around `RankOneFibre`: the genuine chart-reading ideal is mapped
to `B/(read s)`, and that image is definitionally `chartIdealColengthModule`.  Thus a pointwise
span statement for the fibre of the ideal immediately gives the desired vanishing of the
colength fibre.  The span statement is allowed to include the zero-fibre case.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}

namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed

/-- **Pointwise chart-colength fibre vanishing from ideal-fibre span.**  Let `B` be the
pinned-chart section ring, `J` the genuine `B`-ideal generated by the readings of `K`, and
`I = (read s)` for `s ∈ K`.  If every vector of
`κ(p) ⊗[B] J` is a scalar multiple of `1 ⊗ read(s)`, then the image of `J` in `B/I` has
zero `κ(p)`-fibre.  This is the exact single-point input consumed by the `κ(z)` RD-N bridge;
it uses no global base-fibre or flatness inference. -/
theorem subsingleton_chartIdealColengthModule_tensor_residueField_of_ideal_span
    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) (hsK : s ∈ K)
    (p : PrimeSpectrum Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b))
    (hspan : ∀ v : p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[
        Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
        (chartReadIdeal K b), ∃ c : p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
          c • ((1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[
            Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
            (⟨relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s,
              by
                exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩⟩ :
              chartReadIdeal K b)) = v) :
    Subsingleton ((chartIdealColengthModule K b s) ⊗[
      Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
  let B : Type u := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
  let I : Ideal B := Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s}
  let P : Submodule B B := chartReadIdeal K b
  let f : B →ₗ[B] (B ⧸ I) := (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ B I).toLinearMap
  have hsP : relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s ∈ P := by
    exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩
  have hfs : f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0 := by
    change Ideal.Quotient.mk I (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0
    exact Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr (Ideal.subset_span (by simp))
  have hzero := RankOneFibre.subsingleton_map_tensor_of_span_singleton
    P f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) hsP (by
      intro v
      exact hspan v) hfs
  change Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) at hzero
  exact hzero

end ThetaGeneratorSeed

end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	/-!
    10	# Rank-one fibre reduction for the chart colength
    11	
    12	This is the geometric wrapper around `RankOneFibre`: the genuine chart-reading ideal is mapped
    13	to `B/(read s)`, and that image is definitionally `chartIdealColengthModule`.  Thus a pointwise
    14	span statement for the fibre of the ideal immediately gives the desired vanishing of the
    15	colength fibre.  The span statement is allowed to include the zero-fibre case.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
    24	open scoped TensorProduct
    25	
    26	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    27	
    28	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    29	
    30	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    31	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    32	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}
    33	
    34	namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed
    35	
    36	/-- **Pointwise chart-colength fibre vanishing from ideal-fibre span.**  Let `B` be the
    37	pinned-chart section ring, `J` the genuine `B`-ideal generated by the readings of `K`, and
    38	`I = (read s)` for `s ∈ K`.  If every vector of
    39	`κ(p) ⊗[B] J` is a scalar multiple of `1 ⊗ read(s)`, then the image of `J` in `B/I` has
    40	zero `κ(p)`-fibre.  This is the exact single-point input consumed by the `κ(z)` RD-N bridge;
    41	it uses no global base-fibre or flatness inference. -/
    42	theorem subsingleton_chartIdealColengthModule_tensor_residueField_of_ideal_span
    43	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
    44	    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) (hsK : s ∈ K)
    45	    (p : PrimeSpectrum Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b))
    46	    (hspan : ∀ v : p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[
    47	        Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
    48	        (chartReadIdeal K b), ∃ c : p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
    49	          c • ((1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[
    50	            Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
    51	            (⟨relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s,
    52	              by
    53	                exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩⟩ :
    54	              chartReadIdeal K b)) = v) :
    55	    Subsingleton ((chartIdealColengthModule K b s) ⊗[
    56	      Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    57	  let B : Type u := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
    58	  let I : Ideal B := Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s}
    59	  let P : Submodule B B := chartReadIdeal K b
    60	  let f : B →ₗ[B] (B ⧸ I) := (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ B I).toLinearMap
    61	  have hsP : relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s ∈ P := by
    62	    exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩
    63	  have hfs : f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0 := by
    64	    change Ideal.Quotient.mk I (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0
    65	    exact Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr (Ideal.subset_span (by simp))
    66	  have hzero := RankOneFibre.subsingleton_map_tensor_of_span_singleton
    67	    P f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) hsP (by
    68	      intro v
    69	      exact hspan v) hfs
    70	  change Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) at hzero
    71	  exact hzero
    72	
    73	end ThetaGeneratorSeed
    74	
    75	end AlgebraicGeometry

    14	
    15	On the fibrewise h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization
    16	`χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`, the datum engine's `H⁰` is an **invertible** module: finite,
    17	projective, and of stalk-rank exactly `1`.  This is the rank export the engine
    18	(`datumRigidEngine`, `Cohomology/GluedSheafEngine.lean`) leaves open — it delivers
    19	finite + projective, never `rankAtStalk = 1`.
    20	
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_relCurve` — the χ transport `χ(𝒪_{C_L}) = 1 − n` to every
    22	  field `L` of the test tower (base-field invariance of the genus, `chi_moduleKSheaf`
    23	  + `genus_baseField`; a re-derivation of the private lemma of `DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel`).
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one` — **the fibre
    25	  computation**: for a datum whose fibre class over `L` has `classDeg = n`, with `H¹` of
    26	  the base-changed sheaf vanishing, `h⁰(C_L, F_{D_L}) = 1` — the Riemann–Roch anchor
    27	  `h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi` (`n + (1 − n)`) read through the presentation
    28	  bridge `presentationSheafIso`.  The fibre geometric package is threaded as instance
    29	  arguments (`Curve.BaseChangeInstances`).

    32	  `Module.rankAtStalk (H⁰(F_D)) p = 1`.  Route: `Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as
    33	  the `κ(p)`-fibre dimension; `datumH0BaseChange` (on the nose) identifies the fibre with
    34	  `H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`; the fibre computation above pins it at `1`.

    36	  certified-family specialization (**N1**): for `G` landing in the h¹-vanishing locus

   120	    Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf = 1 := by
   121	  set P : (relCurve C L).MeromorphicPresentation :=
   122	    Scheme.MeromorphicPresentation.ofCocycle (D.baseChange L).pointedCover
   123	      (gluedSubordCocycle (D.baseChange L).isGluingCocycle
   124	        (D.baseChange L).pointedCover (D.baseChange L).pieceIndex
   125	        fun _ => le_rfl) with hP
   126	  have hsubP : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (P.gluedSheaf L) 1) :=
   127	    (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L)) 1).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mp
   128	      hsub
   129	  have h0eq : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf = Sheaf.h0 (P.gluedSheaf L) :=
   130	    Sheaf.h0_congr (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L))
   131	  have hformula := h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi L P hsubP
   132	  have hPclass : P.picClass = (D.baseChange L).cechPicClass := rfl
   133	  have hint : (Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf : ℤ) = 1 := by
   134	    rw [h0eq, hformula, hPclass, hg, chi_relCurve hχ L]; ring
   135	  exact_mod_cast hint

   137	/-! ## Σ-RANK1: the rank-1 export on the vanishing locus -/
   138	
   139	/-- **Σ-RANK1, the datum-level rank export** (worksheet GAP-3): on the fibrewise
   140	h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization `χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`,
   141	the datum engine's `H⁰` has stalk-rank exactly `1` at `p`.
   142	
   143	`Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as the `κ(p)`-dimension of the fibre
   144	`κ(p) ⊗[S] H⁰`; the on-the-nose base change `datumH0BaseChange` identifies this fibre with
   145	`H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`, whose dimension is `1` by the fibre computation. The global
   146	fibrewise hypothesis `hfib` supplies finiteness/projectivity (hence flatness) through
   147	`datumRigidEngine`. -/
   148	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one
   149	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C S π) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   150	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   151	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   152	    (hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   153	      Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   154	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
   155	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   156	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   157	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   158	    [QuasiCompact
   159	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   160	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   161	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
   162	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   163	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)]
   164	    (hg : classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   165	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ)) :
   166	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   167	  obtain ⟨-, hfin, hproj⟩ := datumRigidEngine D hπ hfib
   168	  haveI := hfin
   169	  haveI := hproj
   170	  have hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1 := datum_subsingleton_pairH1 D hπ hfib
   171	  have hfibre : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf = 1 :=
   172	    D.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one hχ p.asIdeal.ResidueField hg
   173	      (D.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1)
   174	  calc Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p
   175	      = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   176	          (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)) :=
   177	        Module.rankAtStalk_eq p
   178	    _ = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   179	          (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf 0) :=
   180	        (D.datumH0BaseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1).finrank_eq
   181	    _ = Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf := rfl
   182	    _ = 1 := hfibre
   183	
   184	/-! ## The certified-family specialization: N1 (invertible `H⁰`) and N3 (generators) -/
   185	
   186	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   187	/-- (Implementation) The fibre class of the divisor datum has `classDeg = n` at `κ(p)`:
   188	the base change of `G.eqns`, read through `DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass`. -/
   189	private theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.classDeg_baseChange_divisorDatum
   190	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
   191	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   192	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   193	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   194	    [QuasiCompact
   195	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   196	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   197	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
   198	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   199	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)] :
   200	    classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   201	      (G.adaptation.divisorDatum.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ) := by
   202	  have hcl : G.adaptation.divisorDatum.cechPicClass = (DivFam.mk G).toZar.picClass := by
   203	    rw [G.adaptation.cechPicClass_divisorDatum, DivFamZar.picClass_toZar, DivFam.picClass_mk]
   204	  rw [G.adaptation.divisorDatum.cechPicClass_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField, hcl,
   205	    ← DivFamZar.picClass_mapAlg]
   206	  exact DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass
   207	    (DivFamZar.mapAlg p.asIdeal.ResidueField n (DivFam.mk G).toZar)
   208	
   209	/-- **N1 — invertibility of the canonical `H⁰`** (worksheet §2 (N1)): for a certified
   210	divisor family `G` landing in the h¹-vanishing locus `V` (`hvan`), the divisor datum
   211	`D_G := G.adaptation.divisorDatum` has `H⁰` of stalk-rank exactly `1` at every prime.
   212	
   213	The fibre-degree hypothesis of `rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one` is discharged uniformly:
   214	the fibre class of `D_G` at `κ(p)` is the base change of `G.eqns`, which has
   215	`classDeg = n` at every field (`DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass`). -/
   216	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one
   217	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   218	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   219	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   220	    (hvan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S, (DivFam.mk G).toZar.IsH1VanishingAt p)
   221	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S) :
   222	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   223	  have hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   224	      Subsingleton ((datumPair G.adaptation.divisorDatum).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   225	    fun q => (G.isH1VanishingAt_toZar_iff q).mp (hvan q)
   226	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   227	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   228	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   229	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   230	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   231	  haveI : QuasiCompact
   232	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   233	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   234	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   235	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
   236	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   237	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   238	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
   239	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   240	  exact G.adaptation.divisorDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one hπ hχ hfib p
   241	    (G.classDeg_baseChange_divisorDatum p)
   242	
   243	/-- **N3 — the generator kit** (worksheet §2 (N3)): since `H⁰(F_{D_G})` is projective of
   244	stalk-rank `1` on the locus, its `κ(p)`-fibre is nontrivial, so a fibrewise-nonzero
   245	**global** section exists on a basic open `D(f) ∋ p` — the Zariski-local generator
   246	(`Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`, the Nakayama-neighbourhood kit of
   247	`Picard/LocalGenerators.lean`). -/
   248	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.exists_fibrewise_generator_divisorDatum
   249	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   250	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   251	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   252	    (hvan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S, (DivFam.mk G).toZar.IsH1VanishingAt p)
   253	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S) :
   254	    ∃ f : S, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ ∃ q : Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0,
   255	      ∀ q' : PrimeSpectrum S, f ∉ q'.asIdeal →
   256	        (q ⊗ₜ (1 : q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   257	            Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0 ⊗[S] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 := by
   258	  have hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   259	      Subsingleton ((datumPair G.adaptation.divisorDatum).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   260	    fun q => (G.isH1VanishingAt_toZar_iff q).mp (hvan q)
   261	  obtain ⟨-, hfin, hproj⟩ := datumRigidEngine G.adaptation.divisorDatum hπ hfib
   262	  haveI := hfin
   263	  haveI := hproj
   264	  have hrank : Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
   265	    G.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one hπ hχ hvan p
   266	  -- rank 1 ⟹ the `κ(p)`-fibre is nontrivial
   267	  have hfr : Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   268	      (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) = 1 := by
   269	    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq]; exact hrank
   270	  haveI : Nontrivial (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S]
   271	      Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) :=
   272	    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos (by rw [hfr]; norm_num)
   273	  have hnt : Nontrivial (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0 ⊗[S]
   274	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   275	    (TensorProduct.comm S _ _).toEquiv.symm.nontrivial
   276	  exact Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective p hnt

     9	/-!
    10	# Rank-one fibre quotients
    11	
    12	If a vector `1 ⊗ s` is nonzero in a one-dimensional fibre `K ⊗[B] M`, then it spans that
    13	fibre.  Consequently, every surjective image of `M` that kills `s` has zero `K`-fibre.
    14	
    15	The mapped-submodule form is tailored to an ideal `J ≤ B`: if the fibre of `J` has rank one,
    16	`s ∈ J` survives in that fibre, and a quotient map kills `s`, then the image of `J` in the
    17	quotient has zero residue-field fibre.  This is purely right exactness of tensor product;
    18	neither flatness nor finite generation over `B` is needed at this step.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	set_option autoImplicit false
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	open scoped TensorProduct
    26	
    27	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    28	
    29	namespace RankOneFibre
    30	
    31	/-- A surjective image has zero field fibre when every source-fibre vector is a scalar multiple
    32	of `1 ⊗ s`, and the image kills `s`.  The spanning hypothesis also covers the zero-fibre case;
    33	no dimension or nonzero-vector assumption is required. -/
    34	theorem subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton
    35	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    36	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    37	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (s : M)
    38	    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, ∃ c : K, c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s) = v)
    39	    (hfs : f s = 0) :
    40	    Subsingleton (N ⊗[B] K) := by
    41	  have hft : Function.Surjective (f.lTensor K) :=
    42	    LinearMap.lTensor_surjective K hf
    43	  have hzero : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, (f.lTensor K) v = 0 := by
    44	    intro v
    45	    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hspan v
    46	    rw [← hc, ← TensorProduct.tmul_eq_smul_one_tmul c s,
    47	      LinearMap.lTensor_tmul, hfs]
    48	    simp
    49	  have hsub : Subsingleton (K ⊗[B] N) := by
    50	    refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
    51	    obtain ⟨x', rfl⟩ := hft x
    52	    obtain ⟨y', rfl⟩ := hft y
    53	    rw [hzero x', hzero y']
    54	  exact (TensorProduct.comm B N K).toEquiv.subsingleton
    55	
    56	/-- A surjective image of a module has zero field fibre if it kills a nonzero vector spanning
    57	the one-dimensional source fibre. -/
    58	theorem subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one
    59	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    60	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    61	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (s : M)
    62	    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
    63	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    64	    Subsingleton (N ⊗[B] K) := by
    65	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton f hf s
    66	  intro v
    67	  exact exists_smul_eq_of_finrank_eq_one hfin hs v
    68	  exact hfs
    69	
    70	/-- If a linear map kills a generator of a one-dimensional source fibre, the fibre of its
    71	range is zero. -/
    72	theorem subsingleton_range_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
    73	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    74	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    75	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M)
    76	    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
    77	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    78	    Subsingleton ((LinearMap.range f) ⊗[B] K) := by
    79	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one f.rangeRestrict
    80	    (LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict f) s hfin hs
    81	  apply Subtype.ext
    82	  exact hfs
    83	
    84	/-- Range specialization of `subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton`. -/
    85	theorem subsingleton_range_tensor_of_span_singleton
    86	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    87	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    88	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M)
    89	    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, ∃ c : K, c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s) = v)
    90	    (hfs : f s = 0) :
    91	    Subsingleton ((LinearMap.range f) ⊗[B] K) := by
    92	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton f.rangeRestrict
    93	    (LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict f) s hspan
    94	  apply Subtype.ext
    95	  exact hfs
    96	
    97	/-- Let `P` be a submodule whose field fibre is one-dimensional.  If `s ∈ P` survives in
    98	that fibre and `f s = 0`, then the fibre of the image `f(P)` is zero.
    99	
   100	For a chart ideal `J` and the quotient map `B → B/(s)`, the conclusion is precisely the
   101	vanishing of the fibre of the image of `J` in `B/(s)`. -/
   102	theorem subsingleton_map_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
   103	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
   104	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
   105	    (P : Submodule B M) (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M) (hsP : s ∈ P)
   106	    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] P) = 1)
   107	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
   108	    Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] K) := by
   109	  rw [← LinearMap.range_domRestrict P f]
   110	  apply subsingleton_range_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
   111	    (f.domRestrict P) (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) hfin hs
   112	  simpa using hfs
   113	
   114	/-- Mapped-submodule specialization of `subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton`.
   115	This is useful when the source ideal fibre may itself be zero. -/
   116	theorem subsingleton_map_tensor_of_span_singleton
   117	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
   118	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
   119	    (P : Submodule B M) (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M) (hsP : s ∈ P)
   120	    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] P, ∃ c : K,
   121	      c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P)) = v) (hfs : f s = 0) :
   122	    Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] K) := by
   123	  rw [← LinearMap.range_domRestrict P f]
   124	  apply subsingleton_range_tensor_of_span_singleton
   125	    (f.domRestrict P) (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) hspan
   126	  simpa using hfs
   127	
   128	/-- Quotienting by a vector that survives and spans a one-dimensional field fibre produces
   129	a quotient with zero field fibre. -/
   130	theorem subsingleton_quotient_span_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
   131	    {B K M : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
   132	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M]
   133	    (s : M) (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
   134	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) :
   135	    Subsingleton ((M ⧸ Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)) ⊗[B] K) := by
   136	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one
   137	    (Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)).mkQ
   138	    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _) s hfin hs
   139	  rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
   140	  exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self s
   141	
   142	end RankOneFibre
   143	
   144	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	# DECIDING THE FORK: what non-injectivity of the unrestricted Abel chart actually costs
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean` makes the fork precise and machine-checked:
    12	`IsChartLocusFibre` implies the Abel chart is a monomorphism, which three headers
    13	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`,
    14	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214`) assert it is not.  Exactly one side is right, and
    15	the guard leaves the deciding statement — non-injectivity — as prose.
    16	
    17	**This file reduces that statement to divisor data.**  The reduction is what was missing: the
    18	Abel chart's app does not take divisors, it takes `D.left`-points, so "two divisors in one
    19	linear system" is not by itself a witness.  Reading `abelChartApp_eq`
    20	(`Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean:105`), a point `x : Y ⟶ D.left` is sent to the **pair**
    21	
    22	  `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl))⟩`
    23	
    24	so a non-injectivity witness owes *two* agreements, not one: the Σ-components `x ≫ D.hom` must
    25	agree before the classes are in the same type at all.  That is the trap the c9b row names.
    26	
    27	## What is proved here
    28	
    29	The reduction, in the direction a witness-builder needs, and its converse:
    30	
    31	* `not_injective_abelSigmaChart_of_points` — from two `D.left`-points over one test with
    32	  **equal structure morphism** and **equal chart value** but distinct as points, the Abel chart
    33	  fails to be injective; `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_points` composes that with the guard to
    34	  refute `IsChartLocusFibre`.
    35	* `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_divFamZar` — the same reduction **reparameterised onto divisor
    36	  families**: two distinct elements of `divFamZar C π n T` with equal chart value.  Here the
    37	  Σ-component hypothesis is not passed in: both points are `(rep.homEquiv.symm sᵢ).left`, whose
    38	  structure morphism is the test's own by `Over.w`, so `hstruct` holds by construction.
    39	  **This is a change of parameterisation, not a strengthening** — the two forms are
    40	  inter-derivable (from the family form, take `T := Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom)` and use
    41	  `rep.homEquiv.injective` for distinctness), so `hstruct` is absorbed by the choice of test
    42	  rather than eliminated.  Its value is that the family form is the shape a divisor argument
    43	  produces, with no scheme-theoretic side condition to discharge first.
    44	* `abelChartApp_inj_iff` — the unfolded shape of injectivity at a test, by `Iff.rfl`.  A
    45	  documentation lemma only: it has no call site below, and `abelChartApp_eq`
    46	  (`Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean:105`) already exposes both components.
    47	
    48	## What is NOT proved here, stated so this file is not over-read
    49	
    50	**Nothing here exhibits a curve on which the hypothesis holds, and no theorem below closes the
    51	fork.**  Every statement here is an implication whose antecedent is open.  What remains is
    52	exactly:
    53	
    54	  for some curve, some test `T`, and some `n`: two *distinct* elements of `divFamZar C π n T`
    55	  whose `chartValue` agree.
    56	
    57	Three things to know before pricing that, and the third is the one that moves.
    58	
    59	1. Over a field test it is the classical `h⁰(𝒪(D)) ≥ 2 ⇒ |D|` has two points.
    60	   `Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` (`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`)
    61	   is the exact boundary: uniqueness holds **at** `h⁰ = 1`, so the hypothesis to arrange is
    62	   `h⁰ ≥ 2`.  It is the statement to contradict, not to apply.
    63	2. The passage from two *divisors* to two distinct *elements of `divFamZar`* is not free: the
    64	   families are a quotient of local-equation data (`DivisorFamilyZar.lean:235`), so distinct
    65	   divisors need not give distinct families until that equivalence is read.  Nothing here
    66	   assumes otherwise.
    67	3. **`n` is not free.**  At `n = g` the chart's own degree calibration makes the *fibrewise*
    68	   linear system a single point for free: over a field `K`, an effective `K`-divisor of degree
    69	   `g` with `Subsingleton H¹` has `h⁰ = 1` exactly (`degAt_chartTwist`'s `+g` discussion in
    70	   `Pic0ChartLocus.lean:178-201`, and the rank anchor
    71	   `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`, `RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`, giving
    72	   `h⁰ = g + (1 − g) = 1`).  So the *fibrewise* form of the headers' reason — a
    73	   positive-dimensional `|D|` — is unavailable at `n = g` wherever `H¹` vanishes.
    74	
    75	**AND HERE IS THE LIMIT OF THAT OBSERVATION, which item 3 must not be read past.**  Every anchor
    76	in item 3 is fibrewise over one field: `CurveDivisor` over `K`, `h⁰` a `finrank` over `K`,
    77	`degAt` evaluated at `overSpec k K`-points.  The obligation is **general-test**: injectivity of
    78	`.app (op Y)` at arbitrary `Y`, and correspondingly distinctness in `divFamZar C π n T` at
    79	arbitrary `T`.  A fibrewise anchor does not settle a general-test statement, and the brick that
    80	would bridge them is *relative* GAP-2 — exactly `ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor`
    81	(`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:140`), which `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:160-161` names as
    82	"the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2" and which **nothing in the tree produces**: no declaration
    83	concludes `s₁ = s₂` for two `divFamZar` sections from an equality of their classes.
    84	
    85	So item 3 **relocates** the fork; it does not shrink it.  What it changes is what a witness
    86	should aim at: a bare "two divisors in one linear system" is the wrong target, because at `n = g`
    87	with `h¹ = 0` there are none fibrewise — so a witness wants a point of the divisor scheme where
    88	`H¹` fails to vanish, or a genuinely relative failure of uniqueness that no fibre sees.  Which
    89	of those two it is, is undecided here.  (The degree-`g`/`h⁰ = 1` link is `ajcr-p4`'s measurement,
    90	I-0888; the fibrewise/general-test caveat is a fresh-context review's, I-0923/I-0924.)
    91	
    92	**A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME FORK, added 2026-07-30
    93	(`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverForcesNonInj.lean`), and it does not go through the carve at all.**  The
    94	discussion above — and the `abel-noninj` row — treat the fork as a question about `DivScheme g`:
    95	does it carry a point where `H¹` fails to vanish?  It is *also* a question coverage answers.
    96	`not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` shows that for a **one-chart** atlas,
    97	`PointwiseCoverage` at any open `V ≠ ⊤` produces a test on which the chart is not injective:
    98	instantiate coverage at the test `D.left` itself and at the *tautological* section, at a point
    99	outside `V`; the coverage witness factors through `V` and the tautological one does not.  No
   100	divisor, no `H¹`, no carve fact enters.
   101	
   102	Two consequences for a lane on this row:
   103	
   104	* the fork's **negative** branch is implied by coverage at any proper `V`, so a witness of the
   105	  kind item 3 describes is not the only way to it — and the composites
   106	  `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` /
   107	  `not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` land it directly;
   108	* the fork's **positive** branch — the one item 3 argues for at `n = g` — now has a *cost*:
   109	  by the contrapositive `not_pointwiseCoverage_of_injective_of_ne_top`, an injective chart
   110	  admits coverage at no proper `V`, and `⊥` is refuted too (`not_coverageContainment_bot`), so
   111	  the seam could then close only at `V = ⊤`.  The two branches are no longer "one kills the old
   112	  route, the other is the cheap outcome": each carries a commitment about `V`.
   113	
   114	Nothing there is discharged — coverage at a proper `V` has no producer — and the general-test
   115	caveat above is untouched: the new route sidesteps it rather than answering it, because it never
   116	needs a fibrewise statement in the first place. -/

   127	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   128	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
   129	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   130	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   131	
   132	noncomputable section
   133	
   134	variable {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)

   137	  = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   138	
   139	/-! ## The exact shape of injectivity at a test -/
   140	
   141	/-- **Injectivity of the Abel chart at a test, unfolded.**
   142	
   143	`abelChartApp_eq` is `rfl`, so injectivity of the app at `op Y` is *literally* injectivity of
   144	the pair-valued map below.  Recorded as an `Iff` on the nose so that a lane attacking either
   145	branch of the fork works with the two components explicitly and cannot silently drop the
   146	Σ-component. -/
   147	theorem abelChartApp_inj_iff (Y : Scheme.{u}) :
   148	    Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y))
   149	      ↔ Function.Injective (fun x : Y ⟶ D.left =>
   150	          (⟨x ≫ D.hom, ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom))
   151	              (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)),
   152	            chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩⟩ :
   153	            (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y))) :=
   154	  Iff.rfl
   155	
   156	/-! ## The reduction, in the direction a witness-builder needs -/
   157	
   158	/-- **Two `D.left`-points over one test with the same chart value refute the certificate.**
   159	
   160	The hypotheses are exactly the two agreements `abelChartApp_eq` demands — equal structure
   161	morphism (`hstruct`) and equal chart value after that identification (`hval`) — together with
   162	distinctness of the points themselves.
   163	
   164	Note `hval` is stated at the *transported* family: once `hstruct` identifies the Σ-components,
   165	both chart values live over `Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom)` and the equation typechecks. -/
   166	theorem not_injective_abelSigmaChart_of_points {Y : Scheme.{u}} (x₁ x₂ : Y ⟶ D.left)
   167	    (hne : x₁ ≠ x₂) (hstruct : x₁ ≫ D.hom = x₂ ≫ D.hom)
   168	    (hval : chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom))
   169	        (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₁ rfl))
   170	      = chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom))
   171	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ hstruct.symm))) :
   172	    ¬ Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y)) := by
   173	  intro hinj
   174	  refine hne (hinj ?_)
   175	  -- both values are Σ-elements over the *same* structure morphism after `hstruct`
   176	  refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext (pic0TypeFunctor C) hstruct ?_
   177	  -- the transport of `x₂`'s family along `mkCongr hstruct` is `x₂` read over `x₁`'s base
   178	  have hmap : (divFunctor C π n).map (Over.mkCongr hstruct).op
   179	        (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ rfl))
   180	      = rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ hstruct.symm) := by
   181	    rw [← rep.homEquiv_comp]
   182	    exact congrArg rep.homEquiv (Over.OverMorphism.ext (Category.id_comp x₂))
   183	  have hnat := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom
   184	    ((chartValueTrans C π n m Z hdeg).naturality (Over.mkCongr hstruct).op)
   185	    (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ rfl))
   186	  refine hnat.symm.trans ?_
   187	  rw [ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, hmap]
   188	  exact Subtype.ext hval.symm
   189	
   190	/-- **Hence `IsChartLocusFibre` is false** — the composite with the landed guard
   191	`not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective` (`Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean:159`).
   192	
   193	This is the deliverable of the fork's negative branch: a witness at ONE test kills the only
   194	non-circular route to `IsChartUniv`, hence to antecedent 1 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`. -/
   195	theorem not_isChartLocusFibre_of_points {Y : Scheme.{u}} (x₁ x₂ : Y ⟶ D.left)
   196	    (hne : x₁ ≠ x₂) (hstruct : x₁ ≫ D.hom = x₂ ≫ D.hom)
   197	    (hval : chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom))
   198	        (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₁ rfl))
   199	      = chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom))
   200	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ hstruct.symm))) :
   201	    ¬ IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg :=
   202	  not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective rep m Z hdeg (op Y)
   203	    (not_injective_abelSigmaChart_of_points rep m Z hdeg x₁ x₂ hne hstruct hval)

   205	/-! ## The divisor-family form: where `rep` does the work -/
   206	
   207	/-- **The obligation stated on divisor families rather than on points.**
   208	
   209	This is the shape the linear-system argument produces: two *families* over one test with equal
   210	chart value.  Transporting along `rep.homEquiv` (a bijection) turns them into two points of
   211	`D.left` over that test, and `Over.homMk`'s structure morphism is the test's own, so the
   212	Σ-components agree by construction rather than by hypothesis.
   213	
   214	So the fork's negative branch reduces to a statement with **no** scheme-theoretic side
   215	condition: distinctness in `divFamZar C π n T` plus equality of `chartValue`. -/
   216	theorem not_isChartLocusFibre_of_divFamZar {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   217	    (s₁ s₂ : divFamZar C π n T) (hne : s₁ ≠ s₂)
   218	    (hval : chartValue C π n m Z T s₁ = chartValue C π n m Z T s₂) :
   219	    ¬ IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg := by
   220	  set x₁ : T.left ⟶ D.left := (rep.homEquiv.symm s₁).left with hx₁
   221	  set x₂ : T.left ⟶ D.left := (rep.homEquiv.symm s₂).left with hx₂
   222	  -- both points have the test's own structure morphism, so the Σ-components agree
   223	  have hs₁ : x₁ ≫ D.hom = T.hom := Over.w _
   224	  have hs₂ : x₂ ≫ D.hom = T.hom := Over.w _
   225	  have hstruct : x₁ ≫ D.hom = x₂ ≫ D.hom := hs₁.trans hs₂.symm
   226	  -- `Over.homMk xᵢ` recovers the slice morphism `rep.homEquiv.symm sᵢ` was, hence `sᵢ`
   227	  have hrec₁ : rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₁ hs₁) = s₁ := by
   228	    refine (congrArg rep.homEquiv (Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_)).trans
   229	      (rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply s₁)
   230	    rfl
   231	  have hrec₂ : rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ (hstruct.symm.trans hs₁)) = s₂ := by
   232	    refine (congrArg rep.homEquiv (Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_)).trans
   233	      (rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply s₂)
   234	    rfl
   235	  refine not_isChartLocusFibre_of_points rep m Z hdeg x₁ x₂ ?_ hstruct ?_
   236	  · -- distinct families give distinct points, `rep.homEquiv.symm` being injective
   237	    intro h
   238	    exact hne (hrec₁.symm.trans ((congrArg rep.homEquiv
   239	      (Over.OverMorphism.ext h)).trans hrec₂))
   240	  · -- the two chart values are `hval` restricted along the identity-on-`T.left` slice
   241	    -- morphism `e`, so naturality of `chartValue` transports it
   242	    set e : Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom) ⟶ T :=
   243	      Over.homMk (𝟙 T.left) ((Category.id_comp T.hom).trans hs₁.symm) with he
   244	    have hfac₁ : (Over.homMk x₁ rfl : Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom) ⟶ D)
   245	        = e ≫ rep.homEquiv.symm s₁ :=
   246	      Over.OverMorphism.ext (Category.id_comp x₁).symm
   247	    have hfac₂ : (Over.homMk x₂ hstruct.symm : Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom) ⟶ D)
   248	        = e ≫ rep.homEquiv.symm s₂ :=
   249	      Over.OverMorphism.ext (Category.id_comp x₂).symm
   250	    have hpull : ∀ s : divFamZar C π n T,
   251	        rep.homEquiv (e ≫ rep.homEquiv.symm s) = divFamZar.map C π n e s := by
   252	      intro s
   253	      rw [rep.homEquiv_comp, rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
   254	      rfl
   255	    have hstep : ∀ (s : divFamZar C π n T) (y : Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom) ⟶ D),
   256	        y = e ≫ rep.homEquiv.symm s →
   257	        chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom)) (rep.homEquiv y)
   258	          = picEtMap C e (chartValue C π n m Z T s) := by
   259	      intro s y hy
   260	      subst hy
   261	      exact (congrArg (chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom))) (hpull s)).trans
   262	        (picEtMap_chartValue C π n m Z e s).symm
   263	    exact (hstep s₁ _ hfac₁).trans
   264	      ((congrArg (picEtMap C e) hval).trans (hstep s₂ _ hfac₂).symm)
   265

     8	/-!
     9	# Coverage at a PROPER `V` forces non-injectivity — so the `abel-noninj` fork is not a
    10	question about the carve
    11	
    12	`Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean` refutes both endpoints of the `V`-interval of
    13	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` and leaves one question: *is the pair (`huniv V`, `hcov V`)
    14	inhabited at any `V`?*  Its `⊤`-end refutation
    15	(`not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_not_injective`) is **conditional** on the Abel chart failing
    16	to be injective — the `abel-noninj` fork, which three file headers assert and no declaration
    17	proves.  That row prices the fork as a question about the *carve*: does `DivScheme g` contain
    18	points where `H¹` fails to vanish?
    19	
    20	**The fork is also answered from the other side, by coverage, with no geometry at all.**  This
    21	file proves it.
    22	
    23	## The argument, and it has no divisor content
    24	
    25	Let `f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf C` be *any* map of big-site presheaves and `V ⊆ X` an
    26	open with `V ≠ ⊤`.  Suppose the restricted family `restrictChart f V` satisfies
    27	`PointwiseCoverage` (`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean`) — the datum antecedent 2 is
    28	reduced to.  Instantiate coverage at
    29	
    30	* the test `X` itself,
    31	* the *tautological* section `f.app (op X) (𝟙 X)`,
    32	* a point `t ∈ X \ V`, which exists because `V ≠ ⊤`.
    33	
    34	Coverage returns an open `W ∋ t` and a point `x : ↑W ⟶ ↑V` whose restricted chart value is the
    35	tautological section restricted to `W`.  Unfolding `restrictChart` (which is `rfl`) and the
    36	naturality of `f` at `W.ι`, that equation reads
    37	
    38	```
    39	f.app (op ↑W) (x ≫ V.ι) = f.app (op ↑W) (W.ι)
    40	```
    41	
    42	and the two arguments are **different**: at the point `t` the left one lands inside `V` and the
    43	right one is `t ∉ V`.  So `f.app (op ↑W)` is not injective.
    44	
    45	Two things are worth noting about what that proof does *not* use.  It never looks at the
    46	divisor scheme, the chart index, the twist, `rep`, or `pic⁰` — only that the coverage witness
    47	factors through `V` while the tautological section does not.  And it is the *same* mechanism as
    48	`not_coverageContainment_bot` (`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`) pushed from `⊥` to an
    49	arbitrary proper open: there the containment was refuted outright because `⊥` has no points;
    50	here it is not refuted, it *costs* non-injectivity.
    51	
    52	## What this decides, stated as a dichotomy
    53	
    54	For a **one-chart** atlas, exactly one of the following holds:
    55	
    56	* the Abel chart is non-injective on some test — the fork's negative branch.  Then `V = ⊤` is
    57	  dead (`not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_not_injective`) and, by
    58	  `restrictedChartFibre_top_iff`, `IsChartLocusFibre` is dead with it;
    59	* the Abel chart is injective on every test — the fork's positive branch, which the
    60	  `abel-noninj` row's re-pricing (2) argues for at `n = g`.  Then coverage **fails at every
    61	  proper `V`** (`not_pointwiseCoverage_of_injective_of_ne_top`), and coverage also fails at `⊥`
    62	  (`not_coverageContainment_bot`).  **AND `⊤` DIES TOO**, which an earlier version of this
    63	  paragraph got wrong in its own favour by saying "the only `V` at which the seam can close is
    64	  `⊤`": the only thing keeping `⊤` alive is
    65	  `not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_not_injective`, which *consumes* the negative branch.  So
    66	  under injectivity the seam is unsatisfiable at **every** `V` — a sharper conclusion than the
    67	  dichotomy was claiming (audit `I-1378`).
    68	
    69	So the fork and the `V`-interval are one question, not two: a lane cannot pick the restriction
    70	repair and stay agnostic about the fork.
    71	
    72	**THE PRECISE LOGICAL FORM, because an earlier version of this paragraph said "*equivalent*" and
    73	that is REFUTED** (audit `I-1379`).  Write `N` for the fork's negative branch and `Q` for
    74	`chart-restrict`'s conclusion "any working `V` is a proper intermediate open".  What holds is
    75	`N → Q`, one direction.  `Q → N` does **not** follow from the three landed facts: `Works ≡ False`
    76	satisfies all of them, satisfies `Q` vacuously, and has `N` false.  It needs the extra premise
    77	`∃ V, Works V` — and `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`'s own §"CORRECTED FRAMING" says that
    78	premise has never been measured at any `V`.  So the honest claim is: `Q` is *implied by* the
    79	fork's negative branch, and would be equivalent to it given an inhabitant of the seam that
    80	nobody has.  Quoting the equivalence without that premise is the "two refutations are not an
    81	inhabitation" error this seam has already made once.
    82	
    83	## The honest limits, stated rather than left for a reviewer
    84	
    85	* **Nothing here is discharged.**  `PointwiseCoverage` at a proper `V` is a hypothesis with no
    86	  producer — it is exactly the open question `chart-restrict` names — and so is its negation.
    87	  Every theorem below is an implication between two open propositions.  What is new is that
    88	  they are *linked*.
    89	* **THE ANTECEDENT IS STRONGER THAN DAT-B COVERAGE, and that is the live vacuity risk here**
    90	  (audit `I-1377`).  The hypothesis is coverage by a **single** chart (`ι = PUnit`).  The landed
    91	  converse `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` (`Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean`) turns it into
    92	  *unrestricted* coverage by that one chart, and thence into the local-surjectivity instance for
    93	  a one-chart atlas — which two of this project's own files say should not hold:
    94	  `Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` ("nothing forces one index to work at every point") and
    95	  `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` (the atlas "may be indexed by `m`" precisely so different
    96	  points can use different charts).  So the hypothesis may well be refutable, in which case
    97	  these theorems are true with an antecedent nothing satisfies.  That does **not** damage the
    98	  dichotomy — it is a statement about one-chart atlases either way — but a lane must not read
    99	  "coverage at a proper `V`" here as DAT-B's coverage.  The multi-index version of the argument
   100	  is open; see the next bullet for why it does not go through as written.
   101	* **The argument is per-chart, and a multi-index atlas can evade it.**  Coverage at a general
   102	  family returns *some* index `i`, not the index whose tautological section was tested; if
   103	  `i ≠ i₀` the two chart values live on different sources and no non-injectivity of a single
   104	  map follows.  So the dichotomy above is for a one-chart atlas — which is what
   105	  `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds and what `IsChartUniv`, `RestrictedChartFibre` and
   106	  `restrictedChartFibre_top_iff` are all stated for — and **not** for `mixedParamChart` at
   107	  arbitrary `ι`.  The multi-index case is open and is *not* claimed here.
   108	* **The conclusion is not free**, and the check for that has to satisfy the theorem's *own*
   109	  binders.  `specSecMap_injective` exhibits a map into the Σ-sheaf that is injective on every
   110	  test — the one named by the tautological section `⟨𝟙 (Spec k), 1⟩` — **out of a source that
   111	  has a proper open** (`bot_ne_top_specObj`).  So `(f, V)` with `V ≠ ⊤` exists at which the
   112	  conclusion fails, hence the theorem is a constraint on the pair rather than a fact about the
   113	  sheaf, and composing with `not_pointwiseCoverage_of_injective_of_ne_top` refutes coverage
   114	  there outright.
   115	
   116	  **AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS BULLET NAMED THE WRONG WITNESS, and the correction is the
   117	  lesson** (audit `I-1377`/`I-1380`).  It cited `restrictChart f ⊥`, injective by
   118	  `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart_bot`.  That is true and **useless here** on two
   119	  counts: the source `↥(⊥ : X.Opens)` has a subsingleton open lattice, so it admits no
   120	  `V ≠ ⊤` and the theorem cannot be instantiated at it at all; and every map out of
   121	  `yoneda.obj ↥⊥` is injective on every test for free, since that presheaf is
   122	  subsingleton-valued — so the cited route through the open-immersion criterion was doing no
   123	  work either.  A non-vacuity witness must live where the theorem quantifies.
   124	
   125	## Main declarations
   126	
   127	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chart_map_ι_apply` — naturality of a chart map at an opens inclusion,
   128	  elementwise, named because three proofs below use it.
   129	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` — **the step**: coverage for
   130	  the family restricted to a proper `V` gives a test on which the *unrestricted* map fails to
   131	  be injective.  Arbitrary presheaf map; no divisor content.
   132	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_pointwiseCoverage_of_injective_of_ne_top` — the contrapositive, which
   133	  is the form the fork's positive branch reads: injectivity confines coverage to `V = ⊤`.
   134	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` and
   135	  `AlgebraicGeometry.not_isChartLocusFibre_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` — the compositions
   136	  at the Abel chart: coverage at a proper `V` kills the `⊤` end and the old route with it.
   137	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_injective_into_pic0Sigma` — the non-vacuity check.
   138	-/

   149	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   150	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
   151	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
